problem: The lead says every case, including backlash, is a static nonlinearity y=f(x) whose output depends only on the present input. Backlash has memory: its output depends on direction and history, and the input-output relation is multi-valued. Section 3 says this explicitly, so the lead contradicts the chapter.
fix: State that saturation and dead zone are static nonlinearities. Describe backlash as a nonlinearity with memory (multi-valued, direction-dependent), not as a static y=f(x).

problem: The equations y=x−b (increasing) and y=x+b (decreasing) are branch equations only after the gap is taken up. Used immediately at a reversal they give a jump of 2b, while the prose correctly says the output holds until the input moves through 2b.
fix: Add the hold condition to the formula: at a reversal, y stays at its last value until the input has moved 2b; then use the appropriate branch equation.
